findings.title: Neck detection misses a neck that closes a copper loop (any trace with a hole)
findings.detail: The neck check only compares how many pieces the trace has before and after erosion. In a trace with a hole, cutting a zero-length neck leaves one connected piece (the loop becomes a C shape), so the piece count does not change. The morphological opening does not catch this case either, because it restores both wide blocks. The result is that a 0.1 mm copper neck produces no violation at all. The Layout data model supports holes: fingerprint() and conductors.py both iterate poly.interiors. So 'completely implements neck detection' is true only for simply-connected copper. The current generator builds traces from unions of rectangles and does not produce holes today, which is why this is major rather than a blocker.
findings.evidence: I added a loop to the DC- trace of generate_layouts(3, seed=3, family='side_by_side', dies_per_switch=3)[0]: leg1 = box(20,maxy,23,maxy+6) mm, bar = box(20,maxy+6,35,maxy+9) mm, leg2 = box(35,maxy,38,maxy+6.1) mm. The bar meets leg2 only along a 0.1 mm shared edge. The result is a Polygon with 1 hole, and check() returns [] (no violations). Control: the same neck with leg2 detached from the trace (no loop) is flagged as ['min_trace_width']. A second control with a 1 mm joint in the loop returns [], which is correct.
findings.suggested_check: Also compare the number of holes before and after erosion (a hole can only disappear under erosion through a wall thinner than the min width), and add a closed-loop neck case to test_min_trace_width_neck.

findings.title: 'No KeyError' covers only a missing source pad; an unexpected die.switch still crashes check()
findings.detail: The change replaces d.pads['source'] with .get and adds die_no_source_pad, which works. However, check() still looks up want[d.switch] and expect[...switch] without a default, and Die does not validate switch. A die whose switch is 'hs' (or anything other than 'HS'/'LS') raises KeyError instead of producing a violation. This behaviour predates the change, but the claim says 'no KeyError' without qualification.
findings.evidence: I replaced one HS die in the side_by_side layout with dataclasses.replace(hs, switch='hs'); check() raised KeyError 'hs'.
findings.suggested_check: Emit a violation for switch values outside {HS, LS} instead of indexing the dict directly.

findings.title: Fixed 0.15 mm wire-start margin contradicts its own rationale for the 0.4 mm wires the generator uses
findings.detail: The comment says the margin is half of a 0.3 mm wire diameter so the bond foot does not overhang the pad. But the generator picks diameters from {0.3, 0.4} mm, and DRC allows up to 0.5 mm. By the comment's own half-diameter logic, a 0.4 or 0.5 mm wire placed at the 0.15 mm margin overhangs by 0.05 to 0.1 mm. A real wedge bond foot is also wider and longer than the wire diameter. The value is labelled a placeholder, but the rule does not scale with w.diameter.
findings.evidence: rules.py lines 39-41 (wire_start_margin = 0.15 mm); halfbridge.py line 101 (diam = rng.choice([0.3, 0.4])); boundary behaviour checked: 0.1499 mm is flagged, 0.15 mm passes.
findings.suggested_check: Make the margin max(wire_start_margin, k * w.diameter), or document that it is diameter-independent.

findings.title: Neck violation location points at the whole trace, not at the neck
findings.detail: For neck violations, `where` is _pt(t.polygon), a representative point of the whole trace, so a user cannot find the neck from the report. The die-terminal clearance message also says 'same-net', but the code applies the clearance to every terminal. That is stricter than the comment and harmless.

independent_checks_performed: Ran `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/drc tests/unit/generate tests/unit/geometry`: 57 passed. Ran `uv run ruff check src/moduleforge tests/unit`: clean.
Ran the DoD one-liner (60 layouts, seed=12345): prints 'ok 60'. All layouts are DRC clean, results are deterministic, and at least 3 families and dies_per_switch {2..6} are present.
False-positive sweep: 400 generated layouts (seeds 1-20, 20 each) gave 0 violations of any rule, including the new neck, clearance and wire-start checks.
Adversarial closed-loop neck on the real DC- trace: check() returns []. This is a missed 0.1 mm neck (see the major finding). An open neck on the same trace, used as a control, is flagged.
Confirmed that both new neck test shapes evade the old opening check (thin area 0.0, 2 pieces after erosion), so test_min_trace_width_neck really exercises the new code.
Other simply-connected neck variants are all flagged min_trace_width: a 1 mm square attached by a 0.1 mm corner overlap, a 1 mm square on a 0.1 mm edge, and a rotated block.
Terminal clearance boundary on the interleaved layout: gap 0.999 mm is flagged die_on_terminal; 1.000 and 1.001 mm are not.
Wire-start margin boundary: dx 0.1499 mm is flagged wire_start; 0.15 and 0.1501 mm are not; a start 0.5 nm outside the pad edge is flagged by the margin clause.

Mutation check by monkeypatching check() to drop net_split and die_no_source_pad: test_net_split[DC+/DC-] and test_die_without_source_pad fail by AssertionError. Without net_split, the split layout is otherwise completely clean (the pieces are exactly 1.0 mm apart, so min_spacing does not fire).
Die with switch='hs': check() raises KeyError.
caveats: The neck-detection part of the claim holds only for copper without holes (simply connected). A zero-length neck that closes a loop is not detected.
'No KeyError' holds only for a missing 'source' pad. A die.switch outside {'HS', 'LS'} still raises KeyError.

The permission policy blocked the three heredoc DoD scripts (T0036 cases, T0028 adversarial cases, and the per-rule mutation sweep), so I could not run them verbatim. I covered their substance with equivalent python -c checks (split nets, both neck shapes, clearance at 0/0.5/0.999/1.0 mm, wire start on the pad edge, missing source pad, a partial mutation check) and through the passing unit tests (the 0.9997 mm stub dead band). I did not reproduce the full 20-rule mutation sweep; the orchestrator's run is authoritative for that.
The die-terminal clearance and wire-start margin values are placeholders, not sourced vendor rules.
